pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered his own reasoning and tied it to his job before being asked: 'that sounds like a very logical progression', then 'I have to sit at a desk quite a bit for work, so it's like, I'm aware of all those mobility issues that's caused from that... the mobility stuff is important to me.' He also volunteered that he had done one of Trevor's free workouts the previous day.

Asked practical mechanics rather than reacting to the content: 'does he have things that he'll recommend, like, you know, if you do have to eat out, does he say, like, stay away from these things and stay to the, like, you know, if you have to eat out, know, get, like, take no bun or something?' He also volunteered that he already fasts noon to nine.

The pillar that sold him. 'Yeah, no, I love the community side. I didn't know there was an app or anything like that. So that's really cool too.' Asked what stood out most: 'having the community of people also going through and doing the workouts, I think that's part of what I love the most about CrossFit and why I was always doing that... when it's a class, it's a whole different thing when it's a community doing the same.' Then: 'knowing that makes me even more excited and more engaged on this.'

anchors.raw: I get 5,000 every two weeks. So, I mean, and I move most of that money just into the stock market
anchors.note: Roughly $130,000 a year with an active habit of allocating surplus to investments. Capacity was never in question; only the timing of liquidity was, which the rep solved in under two minutes.

anchors.raw: I have 3K right there. But that's what I, I mean, I get, I get paycheck every, I get 5,000 every two weeks
anchors.note: A liquidity anchor rather than a value one — $3,000 in savings against a $6,000 ask. Correctly diagnosed and solved with a payment plan matched to his pay cycle and rent date.

anchors.raw: I can't tell you how many gyms I've joined thinking, oh, it's just going to be, you know, if I joined this gym, I'll want to go to the gym again
anchors.note: A repeated history of paying for training environments, all of which failed. Supports both the price and the positioning — he has already spent money on the wrong solution several times.

unmet_demand.want: A way to strengthen an undiagnosed knee problem he has never been able to address
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He said plainly 'I've never found a way to strengthen that knee' and that the injury was never officially confirmed. The programme has no clinical assessment and no rehab pathway; the rep answered with a general connective-tissue claim covering knees, shoulders, lower back and glutes.

unmet_demand.want: Continued access to the community after the six-month coaching period ends
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly — 'do you have access to the community afterwards, or is it, you just lose the coaching, right?' — and the exchange that followed was affirmative but muddled, with no clear statement of what persists after month six.

unmet_demand.want: A clear account of what is in the agreement before signing it
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked 'I'm not missing anything in that contract, am I?' and was told it was straightforward. The terms were never reviewed and a verbal free-extension promise was substituted.
